messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High OOM rate detected on inference-pool-us-east-1 (kv-cache resident pages rising steadily). Incident created: INC-6290. Auto-mitigation recommended: enable kv-evict-sweep.

oncall-rotation: picking this up — taking lead. brief status? :wave:

sara-choi: seeing ~30% pod restarts in the past 15m, latency up ~150ms p95 on hosted API routes. Some 502 spikes. Customer-impact unclear yet.

mike-garcia: we have repeated allocator errors in runtime logs: `allocator: paged_attn_alloc failed: cannot allocate page: OOM` and CUDA errors: `CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED` on node gpu-18. Logs attached below.

anya-patel: past 10m heap-map shows growing resident set in kv cache regions, fragmentation pattern looks like slow accumulation of tiny free slots -> inefficient coalescing. I’m calling this a "silt" pattern (lots of small unusable fragments).

devops-zoe: metrics snapshot: 
- kv_cache_resident_pages: +18% (15m)
- paged_attn_free_slots: decreasing
- pod_restarts: 27 (1h)
Link: https://grafana.redwood/board/kv-cache?from=now-1h

sara-choi: any immediate mitigations we can push to stop the creep before full cluster oom?

mike-garcia: short-term options:
1) Reduce concurrency on affected pools: `PATCH /api/pools/inference-pool-us-east-1` reduce max_inflight to 0.6x.
2) Trigger kv compact API to attempt coalescing: `POST https://admin.internal/kv/compact?pool=inference-pool-us-east-1` (non-blocking).
3) Roll nodes to clear per-GPU allocator state: `kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets` for one node at a time.

lee-kumar: I'm for compact + concurrency cap first, roll nodes only if compaction doesn't arrest growth. We should avoid mass restarts during peak.

anya-patel: running compact now on two probe pods to test impact. Output snippet:
```
2026-03-17T18:02:14Z compacter: scan 0..524288 pages, coalesce 392 small fragments -> freed 1.4GB
2026-03-17T18:02:20Z compacter: compaction-pass complete, reclaimed 1.4GB
```

devops-zoe: compact ran on probe-1 and probe-2. KV resident dropped ~1.7GB combined, paged_attn_free_slots temporarily improved. CPU on compactor spiked to 45%.

oncall-rotation: good. Sara, please coordinate a config change to reduce concurrency on affected service routes (hosted generation). Mike, start rolling a single node as a precaution after we verify compact results.

sara-choi: patching pool concurrency now (applied). Observed p95 downtinged by ~30ms after patch.

mike-garcia: starting controlled cordon/drain of gpu-18 (most OOM logs). `kubectl cordon gpu-18 && kubectl drain gpu-18 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=60`

cust-success-bot: Notified customers with active sessions hitting >500ms p95: acct-1347, acct-5522. Templates: "We're investigating elevated latency for inference; teams are mitigating. We'll update within 30 minutes."

lee-kumar: note: we saw `CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED` on gpu-18 which usually follows resident fragmentation; rolling should clear GPU driver state. Coordinate with infra so we don't overload remaining nodes.

anya-patel: compaction on probe nodes holding for now, but still seeing slow regrowth rate on one backend shard. hypothesis: long-lived KV prefixes (large KV keys) causing persistent small allocations that fragment the slab. Need a longer-term fix: smarter coalescing on free-list and periodic background sweep that coalesces tiny holes.

devops-zoe: applied temporary flag to two canary pods to enable aggressive eviction: `KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.11` and `ATTN_PAGE_REUSE=1`. Monitoring.

mike-garcia: after cordon/drain of gpu-18, restarted container runtime on node and brought it back. No immediate OOM log on restart. Pod distribution evened out.

oncall-rotation: customer impact: degraded latency (p95 +120–180ms) and intermittent 502s for small subset; no total outage. Mitigations in flight: pool concurrency reduced, compaction run, one node rolled, canary pods with aggressive evict enabled.

sara-choi: ops checklist for next hour:
- Watch kv_cache_resident_pages and pod_restarts (Zoe)
- Confirm no new CUBLAS failures (Mike)
- Run background compact sweep on remaining 3 shards at +10m if growth resumes (Anya)
- Notify CS on major regressions (Me)

lee-kumar: I'm taking next shift in 30 minutes. handing off from @oncall-rotation. If condition regresses (pod_restarts > 40 or resident_pages climbs > 10%), escalate to SEV2.

oncall-rotation: handing to @lee-kumar — incident remains at SEV3 for now. Updating INC-6290 timeline and notes.

mike-garcia: leaving a short troubleshooting note for follow-up: consider adding a per-allocation size histogram export (we only surface page counts). histogram would help see if tiny allocation rate correlates with silt formation.

anya-patel: agreed. filed TICKET-8423 to add histograms + background coalescer.

cust-success-bot: Posted update to affected customers: "Mitigations applied, latency improving. We'll confirm stability in the next hour." :white_check_mark:

lee-kumar: acknowledged handoff. will monitor and escalate if needed. signing off for now but reachable. :phone:

end of thread: summary: silt-style fragmentation in paged-attn allocator + KV cache leak -> gradual OOM pressure. Live mitigations: compact, concurrency cap, node roll, canary evict flags. Follow-ups: deeper alloc telemetry + background coalescer.
